rationale: ⲣ̄- + ⲍⲏⲃⲉ (Lyc. = ϩⲏⲃⲉ 'mourning, sorrow,' Crum 657a). Cf. ⲡⲉⲧⲣ̄ⲍⲏⲃⲉ 'the one who laments' as epithet of the Cross of Light hidden and suffering in the All — Manichaean cosmic Jesus patibilis.

proposed_english: the gate of Amente at the upper side
rationale: Compound: ⲡⲣⲟ ('gate') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲉⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲉ (Greek-Coptic Amente, the underworld) + relative ⲉⲧ-ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲧⲏⲛ̄ ('which is at the upper side'). Manichaean cosmographic term for the upper gate of the underworld through which redeemed souls ascend out of death.
ⲁ- (directional) + ⲧⲁϣ ('boundary, border'). Standard Coptic noun in directional construction. The 'boundary of death' = the limit between the realm of flesh and the upper realm.

ⲡⲓ- demonstrative + ϣⲁⲙⲧ ('three') + ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲣⲉ ('of strongholds,' Lyc. ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲟⲣⲉ in glossary). Manichaean cosmological term for the three cosmic strongholds (perhaps fire/water/wind walls) that surround and enclose the world-system.

Decorative/ornamental chapter-marker recurring in this manuscript. Function uncertain — possibly a paragraph/section divider or chapter-number sign. Appears alone at line 28 and within the chapter-title line 29 (twice, framing the title). Preserved as Coptic text.
Lyc. ϩⲱⲱⲥ — 3sg.f reflexive/intensive pronoun corresponding to Sahidic ϩⲱⲱⲥ. Already attested as ⲍⲱⲱϩ (3sg.m) in dialect notes; this entry documents the feminine form.
